answers.input: Can I use my contactless JCB card at Shanghai metro gates? I have not told you my credit limit.

answer.text:
Yes — JCB contactless cards are a published supported scheme for direct tap-to-ride at Shanghai Metro gates. Shanghai extended bank-card tap-to-ride to the whole rail network, including suburban lines, from June 28, 2025, and JCB's June 30, 2025 announcement confirms contactless card payment at subway gates or designated readers in Shanghai (and Beijing), including airport routes, without buying a ticket first.

Conditions to be aware of:
- The card must be an eligible JCB contactless chip card usable in China, with ODA (offline data authentication) capability. Type-B chip cards and cards without ODA are excluded.
- Small-amount PIN-free payment must be enabled, and the card needs sufficient balance or available credit.
- No separate metro activation is needed.
- This is direct gate tapping, not the same as buying a ticket first or binding the card in an app.

Your not stating a credit limit does not mean JCB is unsupported: brand-level acceptance and whether one specific card will transact are two separate questions. If entry fails, you can switch to a transit code; if exit fails after entry, go to the station service center.

Note on evidence: these are saved summaries (reviewed September 2025), not a live check. Network counts in the announcements are historical, and not every JCB card or mobile wallet is guaranteed to work — confirm current card compatibility and PIN-free settings with your issuer.
